title: Fidelity mapper and adaptive proxy exploration for OpenAI Responses parity
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Problem: Customers migrating from OpenAI's Responses API encounter behavioral deltas across streaming events, function/tool call framing, and structured output schemas that break existing integrations and eval suites. Goal: Prototype a lightweight fidelity-mapper + adaptive proxy that can sit in front of our runtime (hosted and dedicated) to translate runtime events into an OpenAI-compatible event stream with a fidelity score and corrective hints. Scope: streaming event reordering, function call boundary normalization, structured-output schema alignment, lossiness scoring. Deliver a prototype, telemetry, and a canary plan. Non-goals: full permanent behavior shim baked into core runtime (this is an exploration/prototype to inform a long-term strategy).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype translates example OpenAI streaming sessions end-to-end with <=1% schema-break regressions on a curated corpus; 2) Telemetry emits per-request fidelity_score, token_delta, and functioncall_normalization_count; 3) Canary on 10% of traffic without customer-facing errors for three consecutive days; 4) Performance overhead measured and documented (target <=12ms median added tail); 5) Runbook and rollback plan documented in Confluence.
comments: 2025-03-01 - Triage: Spike approved by EM and PM. Scope refined to focus on three high-risk compatibility surfaces: streaming event semantics, nested functioncall payloads, and structured-output typed fields.

2025-03-03 - Experiment: Initial event-translator prototype implemented as an outbound proxy module (proto v0). Observed two common failure modes when translating partial tokens into function call frames: premature function boundary emission and missing 'tool' metadata. Logged examples to S3: s3://redwood-internal/resp-interop/spike-20250303/

2025-03-05 - Telemetry note: Introduced fidelity_score heuristic (0-100) combining token_delta, event_order_violations, and schema_mismatch_count. Prototype baseline average fidelity_score=83 on our training corpus of 1.2k sessions.
2025-03-06 - Perf: Proxy adds median +9ms p50 and +22ms p95 on a local microbenchmark with batching disabled. PM requests alternate design that keeps latency budget lower for low-latency workloads.
2025-03-07 - Design review: Priya Menon (Design) suggested exposing fidelity_score and top-3 mismatch reasons in Console for Debugging. Action: Add structured debug blob to tracing output.

2025-03-09 - Decision: Two-path approach agreed in tech review: (A) adaptive proxy layer for rapid customer migration and canarying; (B) longer-term in-runtime shim if opt-in is required for vendor parity. Tracked follow-up: ENG-150321 for long-term contract ledger.

2025-03-10 - QA: Fuzz harness executed against 2k synthetic sessions (mix of streaming/toolcall/schema patterns). Found a deterministic edge where nested JSON arrays inside function arguments cause event-splitting. Filed reproducible test case and temporary mitigation to preserve function payload until explicit EOT token is received.

2025-03-12 - Next steps: 1) Harden proxy to preserve tool metadata (est. 2d); 2) Add per-route canary control and telemetry dashboard (est. 3d); 3) Draft canary runbook and rollback toggle in Console (assignee: Aisha). Links below.
Review notes from PM Jordan Li: ensure canary includes customer set filter and a mechanism for automatic rollback on customer-visible error rate spike >0.5%.
Design feedback from Priya Menon: add an API toggle to surface fidelity_score in Developer Console and to opt-out of proxy for latency-sensitive tenants.
Security note: proxy must preserve KMS-encrypted payloads and must not log PII. Security review requested (see security_review_required).

Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 (proto v0 adaptive-proxy); Confluence draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/ENG/Responses+Fidelity+Mapper+Spike; Test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/interop-fuzz
design_notes: Fidelity scoring: weighted sum of token_delta (40%), event_order_violations (30%), schema_mismatch_count (30%); configurable thresholds per-customer.
Adaptive proxy will try non-destructive transformations first (map field names, normalize event types), and fall back to tagging lossiness with hints instead of dropping data.
Canary plan: phase 1 internal traffic, phase 2 invited customers, phase 3 10% open traffic. Automatic rollback trigger on 3-sigma spikes in 1h error rate or >0.5% customer-visible errors.
Instrumentation: per-request trace id propagation, per-token delta histogram, functioncall_normalization_count, last_error_code.
Tradeoffs: Proxy approach enables fast experimentation but duplicates translation code; long-term goal is to collapse profitable transformations into runtime to reduce p99 overhead.
